questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
An English speaking country 
A well-rated university 
A city I would like to explore and become familiar with its culture

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: If you get the chance to go abroad with Erasmus+ do it!!

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy. The University of Edinburgh sent all necessary information to my email with guidance upon arrival, on how to change courses, get registered with a personal tutor and how to attend events etc.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: CAHSS helped with changing my courses

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Edinburgh can be quite difficult finding housing, but I used different Facebook groups and Spareroom and found a flat with two other students. You will have to start three months before to get an overview of the market, areas and price differences.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: You can't start the process of finding housing too early as most of the flats will only be posted 1-2 months before the move-in date. When you then start, you have to be prepared to act fast as many people are looking for a flat to stay in - get an interview and make sure to see the room online or in person. Make sure to know the price of the flat including additional bills as they are always excluded and can be quite a lot...

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
Places to look:
Spareroom
Zoopla
GumTree
The Meadows Share (Facebook group)

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Arriving in Edinburgh you would have to pick up your student card at the main library, fill out upon arrival and proof of attendance form which CAHHS needs to sign, and then have a short meeting with your personal tutor. Everything is explained through emails you will receive from Edinburgh University and else, CAHHS is the one's to contact.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: CAHHS is really helpful!

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got 2 out of three of the classes I wanted after CAHHS helped me switch.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Read thoroughly through the emails, and if you have any questions, contact CAHHS or your personal tutor.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
Unfortunately, my exchange was influenced by industrial act strikes which meant that our classes were canceled for 3
weeks...Some
of the classes were still online due to Covid, but besides that, I really enjoy the academic programs.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took one first-year undergraduate class in History which was all pre-recorded lectures and the level of the Cours was quite fitting. I had two other third-year courses in ECA and the level of both courses was also fitting, sometimes challenging, but I learned a lot and the classes were very well structured.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: At the University of Edinburgh, the classes I had in person were based on a lecture from the teacher, but they also incorporated discussions and exercises to change it up. I had one tutorial class per week in my History course which was really helpful to discuss and get to understand the content of the week's lectures.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Sinner, Saint and Seers: Scottish, Irish and English Art from 600-900.
Orientalism and Visual Culture.
The History of Edinburgh: From Din Eydin to Festival City.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
If you would like to get to know something about the history of Edinburgh, the History course is a good starting point as you get to know the city, buildings, and areas through the lectures and then apply the knowledge when walking around. 

The two art courses are really good. I knew about Orientalism before coming to Edinburgh, but my teacher used different artists and aspects which helped broaden my knowledge and interest in the matter. Sinner, Saints, and Seers is a cool course if you like looking at illuminated manuscripts, medieval treasures, and stone crosses and have an interest for Christian, Roman and Celtic religion, traditions and how it all influence the insular world!

questions.answer: As you are on an exchange, you would (and should) explore the country you are living in. Eventbrite and the University of Edinburgh made a lot of trips to the highlands etc which is really worth going on!!

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
All busses in Edinburgh costs 1,8GBP which is quite good. 
Coffee is a bit less expensive than in Copenhagen.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Everything!! There's a society for everything, a sports club, and activities - just search for it!

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Sign up for the Pleasance Gym - its a standard gym, but you can also do classes, play squash and go bouldering or go to the swimming pool! Play tennis in the Meadows, a court is 10GBP and you can be as many people as you like.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Go to the highlands - you can't be in Scotland without..! 
Go to the markets - Saturday in Grassmarket and Leith, Sunday in Stockbridge.
Explore the city by foot - everything in Edinburgh is in walking distance and the best way to get around is by walking!
Go to the beach in Portobello or North Berwick.
Climb Arthurs Seat and the Craigs. 
Go second-hand shopping - Edinburgh has the best ones!!!
Take a day-hiking trip to the Pentlands - the bus leaves from Edinburgh. 
Eat your way through the city and get some pints!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy as the culture is close to the Danish

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go to as many events at the beginning of the year as you can through the university, go to a pup or get yourself a local coffee bar and talk to the people working!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Scotland is known for their pup culture, be prepared to drink a lot of pints and get "heavy steaming"!

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The kindness and easy going vibe.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. It all seems like too much effort at the beginning with paperwork and getting to know the university and people, but it is all worth it in the end! 

2. CAHHS and your personal tutor is your best friend - use them if you have any questions!

3. Check the format of your course exam before applying for it - some courses have a lot of course work and others a more end-exam based.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Get to know the different campuses - Edinburgh University is huge and is spread all over the city!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Learning about a new culture, meeting lovely people and exploring the country.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Finding a solid group of people to hang out with and adapting to writing in English.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: GO FOR IT!!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
